title: UN Fact-Finding Mission: Venezuela's Repressive Apparatus Remains Intact Despite Limited Reforms
detail: The UN Independent International Fact-Finding Mission on Venezuela published its most comprehensive report to date, finding that despite Nicolás Maduro's January 3 capture and subsequent political changes, the state institutions responsible for repression and crimes against humanity remain largely intact. The Mission documented 214 arbitrary detentions for political reasons between September 2025 and July 2026 (94% before Maduro's removal), plus 64 new torture cases identified after January 3 — including forced intubation and prolonged confinement in a sealed underground cistern at El Rodeo prison, and prisoners held in pit-like cells dug below ground at the Fuerte Guaicaipuro military facility. Independent NGOs estimate 379–500 people remain in political detention, down sharply from pre-transition levels but still substantial. Mission Chair Sofía Macher said 'the reduction in some of the harshest forms of repression is notable, but it does not yet amount in any way to a transformation of the system that made them possible,' while expert María Eloisa Quintero called for accountability to replace 'years of entrenched impunity.' The report gave its most detailed analysis yet of pro-government armed 'colectivos' and their institutional links to the state, and highlighted the case of street vendor Víctor Quero Navas, who died in custody in 2025 — his mother spent 16 months searching for him before learning of his death.

media.caption: The UN Fact-Finding Mission's report found Venezuela's repressive apparatus remains largely intact despite Maduro's removal

title: Trump Removes Venezuela From US 'Failed Demonstrably' Drug-Control Blacklist
detail: President Trump's annual Presidential Determination on Major Drug Transit or Major Illicit Drug Producing Countries, released September 16, removed Venezuela from the list of countries that have 'failed demonstrably' to meet international drug-control commitments — the first such removal for Venezuela in more than two decades. Trump's determination stated: 'Given the positive advances achieved under the leadership of Interim President Delcy Rodríguez, I have determined that Venezuela should no longer be designated as having failed demonstrably.' Venezuela remains listed as a major drug transit country for fiscal year 2027, and the administration said it expects continued, measurable progress from the interim government in dismantling narco-trafficking networks. The decision follows Maduro's January capture and the killing of gang leader José Antonio Tovar ('El Niño Guerrero'); Trump indicated he may consider similar treatment for Colombia.

media.caption: Trump's FY2027 drug transit determination cited 'positive advances' under Interim President Delcy Rodríguez
